hook.line: Simón has been fed bread again, and Tomás has asked three times already. Spanish has a ready-made way to say it for the fourth time, and nobody expects a number as the answer.
hook.es: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que no le des pan a Simón?
hook.en: How many times do I have to tell you not to give Simón bread?

examples.es: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierres la puerta?
examples.en: How many times do I have to tell you to shut the door?

examples.es: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que no le des pan a Simón?
examples.en: How many times do I have to tell you not to give Simón bread?

examples.es: ¿Cuántas veces les tengo que pedir que bajen la voz?
examples.en: How many times do I have to ask you all to keep your voice down?

examples.es: Por última vez, apaga el televisor.
examples.en: For the last time, turn off the TV.

rule:
This is a complaint, not a question. The speaker expects no number.

*¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que* + the order as a *que* form: *cierres*, *bajes*, *no le des*.

The order is a wish, so the verb after *que* changes its vowel (*cierras* becomes *cierres*). Use *les* for a group, *le* for someone you call *usted*.

Shorter and sharper: *Que te sientes, te dije.* The order comes first, with *que*, then *te dije* ("I told you").

The last resort: *Por última vez* and a plain command: *apaga el televisor*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the verb after *decir que* here the subjunctive of an indirect command.

readAndPick.es: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierres la puerta?
options: How many times do I have to tell you to shut the door?
How many times have you told me you shut the door?
How many times will you shut the door?

readAndPick.es: ¿Cuántas veces les tengo que pedir que bajen la voz?
options: How many times do I have to ask him to keep his voice down?
How many times do I have to ask you all to keep your voice down?
How many times do I have to ask you to keep your voice down? (to one friend)
I sat down, you told me.
He told me to sit down.
Sit down, I said.

readAndPick.es: Por última vez, apaga el televisor.
options: For the last time, turn off the TV.
For the last time, I turned off the TV.
The TV was turned off for the last time.

readAndPick.es: ¿Cuántas veces le tengo que decir que no toque eso, señor?
options: How many times do I have to tell you not to touch that, sir? (to a friend)
How many times do I have to tell you not to touch that, sir? (formal)
How many times do I have to tell him he touches that, sir?

readAndPick.es: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que no le des pan a Simón?
options: How many times do I have to tell you that you gave Simón bread?
How many times do I have to tell you to give Simón bread?
How many times do I have to tell you not to give Simón bread?
Be quiet, I said.
You asked me to be quiet.
I'm being quiet, you said.

readAndPick.es: Que no lo toques, te dije.
options: You said you didn't touch it.
Don't touch it, I said.
Touch it, I said.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *cierro* or *cierres*, then type the whole sentence: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que ___ la puerta?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierres la puerta?
yourTurn.why: An order after *decir que* takes the *que* form, *cierres*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Sit down, I said. (to a child)
yourTurn.why: Put the order first with *que*, then *te dije*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: How many times do I have to tell you all to keep your voice down?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cuántas veces les tengo que decir que bajen la voz?
yourTurn.why: A group takes *les* and the *-n* form, *bajen*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: For the last time, turn off the TV. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Por última vez, apaga el televisor.
yourTurn.why: After *por última vez* comes a plain command.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: How many times do I have to tell you not to give Simón bread? (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que no le des pan a Simón?
yourTurn.why: *No* comes before the verb, and *des* is the *que* form of *dar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal, to someone you call *usted*: *¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierres la puerta?* becomes the same complaint to a stranger.
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cuántas veces le tengo que decir que cierre la puerta?

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Be quiet, I said. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: Same frame: the order with *que*, then *te dije*.

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierras la puerta?
pitfalls.right: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierres la puerta?
pitfalls.why: Almost. An order is a wish, so the verb takes the *que* form: *cierres*.
The verb is *sentarse* (to sit), so *te sientes*. *Sientas* belongs to *sentir*, to feel.

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cerrar la puerta?
pitfalls.right: ¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que cierres la puerta?
pitfalls.why: English says "to shut", but after *que* Spanish needs a conjugated verb.

personal: Think of something that someone at home never does without a reminder. Say your complaint with *¿Cuántas veces te tengo que decir que…?*
